speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the onset of your symptoms and whether there is any history of trauma or insect bites on your right ring finger. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal CBC and ESR results, which makes an acute infection or systemic inflammatory process less likely. Do you recall any specific event, such as a minor injury, a thorn prick, or exposure to a plant or insect, around the time the swelling began? REQUEST IMAGES: Right finger ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic "Jersey Finger" injury where the flexor tendon avulses from the distal phalanx. Given the normal inflammatory markers, I want to confirm if you have any loss of active flexion at the tip of that finger when you try to curl it? REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP, Lateral, Oblique).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion fracture of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus tendon).

Please confirm: Can you actively flex the distal phalanx of the right ring finger at all, or is it completely immobile compared to your other fingers? REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP, Lateral, Oblique) [Repeat if not fully reviewed to look for avulsion fragment].

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
